newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak banks, NBS to cut volume due to volatility.
newsitem.headline: Slovak banks, NBS to cut volume due to volatility.

text.p: The National Bank of Slovakia (NBS) and eight reference banks on the money market have agreed to temporarily cut their minimum quoted volumes due to interest rate volatity, dealers said on Wednesday.

"Until recalled, the reference banks will continue to cumpulsorily quote currently lower volumes, by half, due to worries of the interest rate volatility, which may follow the current liquidity outflow," Martin Hrozany, chief dealer at Slovenska Sporitelna, told Reuters.
Rates from three- to six-months are most commonly used to determine instruments such as swaps and forwards.

"Some banks appear scared of a liquidity insufficiency or uncertainty, but I think the agreement itself adds to uncertainty. Thus, it is a mistake to quote lower volumes," said Rastislav Zivor, a dealer with ING Bank.

The liquidity cruch, which had prompted the agreement along with a boost in Slovak interbank money market rates to record highs of 26 percent in January, has since been relaxed by an estimated $130-380 million inflow.
On Tuesday, the NBS said most of the inflow had already been pulled out of Slovakia.
Interbank money market rates rose on Wednesday an average 150 basis points on short terms, and some 50 basis points on longer terms to a range of 17.5-19 percent, flattening the yield curve.
Dealers said they expected the rise to level out at 20 percent due to the outflow. They were also eyeing the central bank for some kind of interest rate intervention.
